Martin Lau laid out a clear case for why AI capex should moderate after 2027:

1/ Front-loaded investment: AI infrastructure is like building a factory. Once built, it can continuously train new models and generate tokens.

2/ Lower hardware costs: The same equipment should cost significantly less by 2028.

3/ Rapid efficiency gains: The same infrastructure can deliver exponentially more training compute and token output over time.

Takeaway: Martin is effectively calling for a peak in AI capex in 2026-27, with a meaningful decline in capex intensity thereafter, even as AI demand continues to grow.

The read-through for semis is interesting: If annual industry AI capex eventually normalizes below $1T, assigning a mid-range multiple to normalized earnings, that’s your industry total size.

zh_summary: NVDA Q3 FY27: BEAT and raise. Last week I called Jensen's exit a stock shock, n.
en_summary: NVDA Q3 FY27: BEAT and raise. Last week I called Jensen's exit a stock shock, n.
text:
$NVDA Q3 FY27: BEAT and raise. Last week I called Jensen's exit a stock shock, not a business shock. NVIDIA raised its FY28 outlook. Exactly as I said. 

The numbers:
-Revenue $115.8B, +103% YoY, vs $109.1B est: BEAT
-Non-GAAP EPS $2.68 vs $2.48 est, $2.60 whisper: BEAT
-Non-GAAP gross margin 74.9% vs 74% guide: BEAT. Q4 guide ~71.5% vs 71.7% est: MISS
-Q4 guide ~$130B vs $125.3B est: BEAT

Takeaways:
1. FY28 growth outlook: ~75%, from 70%. ~$741B by my math vs $692B street: BEAT.
2. The $130B guide is +12% QoQ, like the Q3 guide. Q4 has 14 weeks, so per week, ex-China, it's half: +6%. FY28's +75% needs ~18% a quarter. My math.
3. Monday I said we might hear Kress's sort order. We did: suppliers first, customer financing selective. Supply commitments: $390B.
4. Q4 is the gross margin bottom, as guided in August. FY28 stays below Q3 despite price increases: NVIDIA eats part of the memory bill.
5. In May I wanted a clearer picture of the Rubin ramp: ~$20B in its first shipping quarter, as guided.

@nvidia

Interim CEO Colette Kress opened with: 
“Our momentum is real.”
She wasn’t kidding. 

Here’s what they said:
Guidance
• They raised FY28 revenue growth to ~75%, up from 70%, on a bigger FY27 base. That’s roughly $740B of revenue next year
• Q4 is guided to $130B
• Colette said Q4 is the bottom for gross margin, and they expect 72–73% in FY28

Vera Rubin
• Nearly $20B of revenue in its first quarter of shipments, the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA’s history
• Hyperscalers brought Rubin into production in about a month, half the time Grace Blackwell took
• Rubin Ultra comes next year and Feynman in 2028

Pricing power
• They said Hopper GPUs are being recontracted at up to 2x their original price
• B300 rental rates are up 60%+ since launch
• Every hyperscaler and neocloud they serve is running NVIDIA compute at full utilization

Demand is everywhere
• Networking alone did $21B+ in the quarter
• Sovereign AI revenue more than tripled y/y
• Physical AI is on track for $25B+ this year
• They expect CPU revenue and enterprise revenue to each more than double in FY28
• Cloud industry backlog is $2.5T, up from $2T three months ago
